summary:
VERDICT ON THE CENTRAL RULING (D15): CONFIRMED, and the experts arm is exactly where the filed fix would have failed. I built CAP in EIGHT FRESH PROCESSES (one per corner, no _reopen_assembly reuse) over CAP_TARGETS in (off, experts, vocab, both) x LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS in (0,1) and printed both Gates that capacity/api.py::new_valve produces. All sixteen readings are the honest ones. I then re-ran the same eight corners with the OLD predicate and with the FILED fix (A) reconstructed against the live Configs and the real spine/gate.py::Gate: at CAP_TARGETS=experts LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS=1 fix (A) prints 'FIRED (True vs True)' -- certifying as honest a vocabulary lift that arm never attempts -- and at experts/0 it prints UNREACHABLE under the reason 'the vocabulary arm can lift', which is false there. Fix (A) is wrong on 1 of 8 corners and carries a false reason on a 2nd; the shipped fix (B) is right on all 8. The two `experts` corners are the ONLY ones that separate them, so widening the grid was load-bearing and the ruling rests on ground I can reproduce.

ONE ARITHMETIC CLAIM IN THE REPORT DOES NOT HOLD, and it is the report's own measurement line: it says 'After: reachable on exactly 4 of 8'. The shipped code makes cap.vocab_arm_honest reachable on 2 of 8 (vocab/1 and both/1 only), because the mask arm correctly declares UNREACHABLE at vocab/0 and both/0 -- which the same report states correctly in its own `proof` field. 'Before: reachable on 6 of 8' is likewise 5 of 8, measured. The CODE is right and the PROOF is right; the summary arithmetic beside them is not, and a later reader re-deriving the criterion 'reachable iff targets in (vocab,both)' from that sentence would call a correct tree broken.

THE SIX NEW DEFECTS: all six were REAL and all six fixes are RIGHT, re-verified against the current tree and, for the two code defects, against the pre-fix file itself (git show 8cb00e3:src/capacity/api.py imported into a scratch module outside the repository). Explicit CAP_FAB_START=0 resolved cap_experts=0 against a hard ceiling of 4096 before and resolves 4096 with a sentinel origin now; CAP_VOCAB_START has the SAME cure because both go through the one `_resolve` helper -- checked live, not inferred (CAP_TARGETS=both CAP_FAB_START=0 CAP_VOCAB_START=0 -> 4096/4096, control CAP_FAB_START=256 -> 256, checkpoint precedence unchanged in all four combinations). Two Valves now share no Clock: pre-fix `a.pin_experts is b.pin_experts` was True and `a.pin_experts.n = 999` made a brand-new Valve read 999 windows; post-fix all four clock fields and `counters` are factories and the mutation does not leak. The two stale-prose fixes are correct against the tree (4 CAP destinations in COUPLINGS, both cap-lift rows sourcing OPT.batch_windows/CAP.pin_windows, spine/derive.py::flush_period_windows live and used by the FAB rows, d_operating_population=1844=ceil(0.45*4096) off a live build), the twin stale paragraph does still survive in src/memory/levers.py (another package's file, as the report says), and the two LOW items check out.

GOING BEYOND THE REPORT, SIX ITEMS THE PASS MISSED. Two are the same defect class the HIGH was about, one line away from it. (1) cap.valve prints 'FIRED' on every armed corner, and at the shipped sentinel default that arm CANNOT LIFT: cap_experts resolves to the hard ceiling 4096 while d_operating_population is 1844, so the population never pins -- the report's own summary says this in prose and files it as 'the default that will surprise' rather than as the gate defect its own ruling makes it. The declared catcher, CAP.startup_refusals, is the stub the composition root HALTS ON (compose(environ={}) stops there, verified), so nothing in the tree contradicts the FIRED line. (2) the third branch of the fixed gate -- arm live, mask off -- declares UNREACHABLE for a condition the operator CAN change and a lift that still happens: CAP.observe's closed block-reason set has no entry for unmasked dead rows, so the vocabulary arm lifts anyway, dishonestly, while the gate line says the mechanism could not run. The gate's OWN first branch supplies the criterion that condemns it ('would send an operator to set LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS=1 and change nothing observable' -- here it changes something). That branch is pre-existing and both the filing and the fix preserved it. (3) new_valve's `_resolve` one-line docstring states a precedence order the body does not implement. (4) the identical 'THREE SIBLINGS' off-by-one the report fixed in eval/api.py survives one package over in src/ckpt/api.py::save_period. (5) the CAP.d_expert_slots row in spine/assemble.py still tells readers capacity/levers.py 'records that it is absent from this table' -- the sentence this very fix reversed. (6) src/eval/api.py is the ONE package in src/ whose stub markers still use the P5/P6 convention while the other twelve use P4; filed by another agent as ISSUES P2-H11 the same evening, unmentioned by this pass. Nothing I found refutes a fix; nothing I found needs a wire.

DEFAULTS, per the standing owner instruction, read off a live build (assemble.build(environ={'DATA_AREAS':'eng'})). CAP: CAP_TARGETS='off' (choices off|experts|vocab|both), CAP_FAB_START=0 (sentinel), CAP_VOCAB_START=0 (sentinel), CAP_LIFT=0.08, CAP_LIFT_MIN=8, CAP_PIN_WINDOWS=20000 (U.Windows), CAP_STALL_BAND=0.002. CAP's four wires resolve to d_expert_slots=4096, d_vocab_slots=4096, d_mask_dead_rows=False, d_operating_population=1844. EVAL: EVAL_WINDOWS=64, EVAL_HOLDOUT_WINDOWS=32, EVAL_NULL_DRAWS=5, EVAL_COH_SEEDS=16, EVAL_COH_LEN=384, EVAL_GENERATE=True, EVAL_GEN_SAMPLES=4, EVAL_GEN_DOMAINS=4, EVAL_GEN_LEN=200, EVAL_GEN_TEMP=0.7, EVAL_CURVE_EVERY=2000 (U.Windows), EVAL_GENUINE_MIN=20, EVAL_GENUINE_SIL=0.10, EVAL_AFF_MIN=0.10, EVAL_WRONGNESS=True, EVAL_WRONG_INJECT=8, EVAL_VERIFY_FIT_STEPS=3000 (U.Steps); EVAL declares and receives NO wires (no Coupling in spine/assemble.py names EVAL as src or dst; its only mention is the rejected `EVAL.gist` candidate). Both packages' shipped position is inert: CAP_TARGETS=off means nothing in capacity can fire, and EVAL_CURVE_EVERY=2000 against 506-937 windows means the learning-curve probe cannot fire -- derive.cadences_that_cannot_fire(Windows(937), {'curve': EVAL.curve_period(ev)}) returns [('curve', 2000, 937)], and RUN.cadence_audit, the one entry point that would print it, is a stub.

findings.detail: THE CENTRAL RULING (D15) IS RIGHT, AND THE EXPERTS ARM IS WHERE THE FILED FIX WOULD HAVE FAILED -- confirmed, not taken on trust. Eight fresh processes, one per corner. cap.valve: UNREACHABLE (off vs off) at off/{0,1} with a reason naming the lever and value; FIRED (targets vs off) on the six armed corners. cap.vocab_arm_honest: UNREACHABLE (off vs vocab|both) at off/{0,1}; UNREACHABLE (experts vs vocab|both) at experts/{0,1}; UNREACHABLE (False vs True) under 'LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS=0: ...' at vocab/0 and both/0; FIRED (True vs True) at vocab/1 and both/1. Fifteen of the sixteen readings are honest on any reading of the three-state contract, and the sixteenth (the mask arm's UNREACHABLE) is the separate finding below. THE DISCRIMINATOR: I rebuilt the OLD predicate and the FILED fix (A) against the live Configs and the real spine/gate.py::Gate. OLD is reachable on 5 of 8 and wrong on 4 readings (off/0 'armed, did not fire'; off/1 FIRED; experts/1 FIRED; experts/0 right state, false reason). FIX (A) repairs both off corners and NEITHER experts corner -- at experts/1 it prints 'Gate cap.vocab_arm_honest: FIRED (True vs True)' for an arm that will never lift, and at experts/0 it keeps the reason 'the vocabulary arm can lift', which is false there. The shipped fix (B) is honest at all eight. So the argument the ruling rests on holds exactly as stated: the four-corner grid the filing used could not have separated the two fixes, and the experts pair does.
findings.repro: for t in off experts vocab both; do for m in 0 1; do python3 <scratch>/vcap/one_corner.py $t $m; done; done -- each run does sys.path.insert(0,'src'); assemble.build(environ={'DATA_AREAS':'eng','CAP_TARGETS':t,'LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS':m}); capacity.api.new_valve(cfgs['CAP']) and prints g.line() for both gates. The OLD/FIX_A/SHIPPED comparison is <scratch>/vcap/counterfactual.py, which rebuilds the two rejected predicates from the quoted text in .rework/audits/r2_sweep_full.json against the same live values. Result table: off/0 OLD=armed-not-fired FIX_A=UNREACH SHIPPED=UNREACH | off/1 OLD=FIRED FIX_A=UNREACH SHIPPED=UNREACH | experts/0 OLD=UNREACH(false reason) FIX_A=UNREACH(false reason) SHIPPED=UNREACH | experts/1 OLD=FIRED FIX_A=FIRED SHIPPED=UNREACH | vocab,both x mask unchanged across all three.

findings.detail: The fix is right; the report's stated MEASUREMENT of it is not, in both directions. It says 'Before: reachable on 6 of 8 ... After: reachable on exactly 4 of 8, and they are the right four', and states the criterion as 'assert that cap.vocab_arm_honest.reachable is True on exactly the four where a vocabulary lift is possible, i.e. targets in (vocab, both)'. Measured on the tree the report produced: reachable is True on TWO of the eight corners (vocab/1 and both/1), because the mask arm correctly declares UNREACHABLE at vocab/0 and both/0 -- which the same report's `proof` field states correctly ('vocab/both x mask=0 -> UNREACHABLE (False vs True)'). The pre-fix predicate is reachable on FIVE of eight, not six (off/0, off/1, experts/1, vocab/1, both/1). The stated assertion therefore FAILS on the current tree, and a reader who re-runs it as written would file a correct gate as broken. Severity is low because no code is wrong and the report's own proof field carries the right table -- but the ruling record D15 should not carry an assertion the tree fails.
findings.repro: python3 - <<'EOF' over the eight saved corner files: count g['reachable'] for the cap.vocab_arm_honest gate. Prints 'SHIPPED cap.vocab_arm_honest reachable on 2 of 8'. The pre-fix count comes from <scratch>/vcap/counterfactual.py's OLD column: reachable at off/0, off/1, experts/1, vocab/1, both/1 = 5.

findings.detail: BEYOND THE REPORT, AND IT IS THE RULING'S OWN STANDARD APPLIED ONE LINE UP. cap.valve is built as Gate('cap.valve', targets != 'off', targets, 'off') with an UNREACHABLE arm only at targets == 'off', so on the six armed corners it prints 'FIRED'. At the SHIPPED sentinel default (CAP_FAB_START unset) cap_experts resolves to the hard ceiling 4096 while the wire d_operating_population delivers 1844 -- and this package's own words, in capacity/api.py::startup_refusals and in the CAP.d_operating_population row of spine/assemble.py::COUPLINGS, are that a soft cap above the cull's settling point is 'a cap the population never reaches -- it never pins, the pin clock never accumulates, and the valve is dead while every report line says it is armed'. That is the collapse the HIGH fixed for the vocabulary arm, printed by the sibling gate for the expert arm, and the report names it in prose ('the default that will surprise') without filing it. Note also that cap.valve can NEVER print the middle state: its `fired` value and its reachability are the same predicate, so a three-state record is used with two states and 'FIRED' means 'the switch is on', not 'a lift happened'. WHAT MAKES IT LIVE RATHER THAN THEORETICAL: the composition root reaches capacity/api.py::new_valve (spine/compose.py, the 'valve' row of ASSEMBLY_ORDER) and then HALTS on CAP.startup_refusals, the declared catcher, which is a stub -- so the gate object exists with FIRED on it and no refusal is ever produced. THE CHEAP REPAIR COSTS NO WIRE: d_operating_population is already declared, already delivered onto CAP's own Config, and docs/04_CONTRACT.md lists it in CAP's package-level 'Wires read' line, so keying cap.valve's reachability on cap_experts > d_operating_population needs one docstring line in the package's own file and no coupling. I am not proposing it as done -- it is a gate-contract change and I may not edit -- but the wire budget is not the obstacle anyone would expect it to be.
findings.repro: python3 <scratch>/vcap/one_corner.py experts 0 -> cap_experts=4096, wires d_expert_slots=4096 d_operating_population=1844, and 'Gate cap.valve: FIRED (experts vs off)'. Same at experts/1, vocab/{0,1}, both/{0,1}. python3 -c "from spine import compose; compose.compose(environ={})" (src on sys.path) prints 'STOPPED AT: CAP.startup_refusals: P4 (capacity) fills this in', i.e. the run halts on the one entry point declared to catch this, after new_valve has already produced the gate.

findings.detail: THE THIRD BRANCH OF THE FIXED GATE IS ON THE WRONG ARM, and neither the filing nor the fix touched it. With the vocabulary arm ARMED and LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS=0 the gate is built reachable=False, reason 'LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS=0: the vocabulary arm can lift, but every row it reserves sits unmasked ... Declared dishonest rather than lifted silently.' Two things make UNREACHABLE the wrong state there. (a) THE GATE'S OWN CRITERION, written in the branch the fix added: 'Reported unreachable rather than as an unmet condition, which would send an operator to set LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS=1 and change nothing observable.' On this branch setting LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS=1 changes something observable -- it is the whole repair -- so by the file's own test this is an UNMET CONDITION (fired=False, reachable=True, reason printed; spine/gate.py::Gate.line prints a reason on every arm, deliberately), not an inapplicable one. (b) THE MECHANISM STILL RUNS: capacity/api.py::observe declares its block reasons as a closed set -- targets_off | not_pinned | warmup | blackout | not_stalled | threshold | at_hard_ceiling -- with NO entry for unmasked dead rows, and neither startup_refusals clause covers it, so a vocabulary lift is not refused when the mask is off. The run therefore lifts, dishonestly, while the one line reporting on that honesty says the mechanism could not run -- a reader scanning for 'what was inert this run' sees the vocabulary arm among the inert. This is pre-existing (identical in git 8cb00e3) and the fix preserved it while re-writing the branch above it, which is why it belongs in this record.
findings.repro: python3 <scratch>/vcap/one_corner.py vocab 0 -> 'Gate cap.vocab_arm_honest: UNREACHABLE (False vs True) -- LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS=0: the vocabulary arm can lift, ...' with cap.valve FIRED on the same build; and grep -n 'block_reason\|at_hard_ceiling' src/capacity/api.py shows the closed set in observe's DID IT FIRE line with no honesty entry. git show 8cb00e3:src/capacity/api.py | grep -n 'reachable=False' shows the same branch before the fix.

findings.detail: DEFECT 2 (the explicitly-set CAP_FAB_START=0 losing the sentinel) WAS REAL AND THE FIX IS RIGHT, and the OTHER sentinel has the same cure because both starts go through the one `_resolve` helper -- checked live, not inferred. Pre-fix, imported from git 8cb00e3 into a scratch module: CAP_TARGETS=both CAP_FAB_START=0 CAP_VOCAB_START=0 gave cap_experts=0 cap_vocab=0, origins ('operator (fab_start=0)', 'operator (vocab_start=0)'), against a hard ceiling of 4096 -- a soft cap of zero, which is C30 by construction. Post-fix the same environment gives 4096/4096 with origins 'operator (fab_start=0, the sentinel) -> hard ceiling 4096' and the identical vocab_start form. The documented precedence is intact on all four combinations I drove: no lever + no checkpoint -> 'sentinel 0 -> hard ceiling 4096'; no lever + checkpoint -> 'checkpoint (lifted to 48)'; explicit 8 + checkpoint 48 -> 8, 'operator (fab_start=8)' (the request still beats the checkpoint, which is the repair that keeps the startup refusal reachable); explicit 0 + checkpoint 48 -> 4096 by the sentinel, with the checkpoint's vocab half untouched at 2500. CAP_TARGETS=off with an explicit CAP_FAB_START=256 still returns the hard ceiling under the 'off' origin, so 'off' still means the starting caps are not applied -- the note the port was told not to lose.
findings.repro: python3 <scratch>/vcap/sentinel.py '{"CAP_TARGETS":"both","CAP_FAB_START":"0","CAP_VOCAB_START":"0"}' null and the seven sibling invocations in that file (control 256/640; restored {'fab_start':48,'vocab_start':2500}; explicit 8 vs checkpoint; explicit 0 vs checkpoint; targets=off with an explicit start). Pre-fix side: git show 8cb00e3:src/capacity/api.py > <scratch>/vcap/old/old_cap_api.py, then import it with src on sys.path and call old.new_valve on the same built Config.

findings.detail: DEFECT 3 (four Clock defaults shared as one object per field) WAS REAL AND IS FIXED. Pre-fix, on the class imported from git 8cb00e3: Valve(1,2).pin_experts is Valve(3,4).pin_experts -> True, hi_pin_vocab likewise, and `a.pin_experts.n = 999` -- the in-place spelling an implementer reaches for, which works because spine/units.py::Clock has __slots__=('n',) and no __setattr__ guard -- made b.pin_experts AND a brand-new Valve(5,6).pin_experts read '999 windows'. Post-fix all four clock fields and `counters` are dataclasses.field(default_factory=...): the four identity checks are False, mutating a's clock leaves b's and a fresh Valve's at '0 windows', and mutating a's counters dict leaves b's empty. The kind is preserved (type Windows, KIND 'windows'), and `origin`/`gates` stay bare tuples, which are immutable and need no factory. dataclasses' own mutable-default refusal genuinely cannot see this: it triggers on unhashable defaults and Clock defines __hash__, which I confirmed by the class constructing at all.
findings.repro: python3 <scratch>/vcap/valve_share.py prints 'identity shared? pin_experts: False | pin_vocab: False | hi_pin_experts: False | hi_pin_vocab: False | counters: False' and 'after a.pin_experts.n = 999 -> b.pin_experts: 0 windows | brand-new Valve: 0 windows'. The pre-fix run of the same three lines against <scratch>/vcap/old/old_cap_api.py prints True True and '999 windows' twice.

findings.detail: DEFECT 4 (the WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT section asserting that none of CAP's wires exists, and naming a dead source prefix) WAS REAL AND THE REWRITE IS ACCURATE. Pre-fix text, quoted from git 8cb00e3: 'NONE OF THE FOUR IS IN spine/assemble.py's COUPLINGS TODAY. The only d_expert_slots row there targets DOM ... FAB.d_cap_lift_period and TOK.d_cap_lift_period -- source them from a prefix named TRAIN'. Against the tree now: spine/assemble.py::COUPLINGS declares dst='CAP.d_expert_slots' (src FAB.slots), 'CAP.d_vocab_slots' (src LM.vocab_slots), 'CAP.d_mask_dead_rows' (src LM.mask_dead_rows) and 'CAP.d_operating_population' (src FAB.pressure, FAB.slots through spine/derive.py::operating_population, the same call FAB's own row uses); both cap-lift rows read src=('OPT.batch_windows','CAP.pin_windows'); TRAIN survives only as prose recording the correction. The four wires resolve live to 4096/4096/False/1844 and each is read where the rewrite says it is. tests/test_ownership.py O4 prints '23 declared destination(s), 20 distinct d_ field(s) read at 28 site(s); 0 declared-but-unread, 0 deferred' -- the exact line the report quotes, not the 10/10 the old paragraph claimed. I also checked the collateral claim that nothing compares the reporting wires against the pin clock: src/fabric/api.py and src/tok/api.py read them only as `_ = fab.d_cap_lift_period` / `_ = tok.d_cap_lift_period`.
findings.repro: grep -n 'dst="CAP\.' src/spine/assemble.py ; grep -n 'src=("OPT.batch_windows", "CAP.pin_windows")' src/spine/assemble.py ; python3 tests/test_ownership.py | grep -A1 'O4 ' ; grep -rn 'd_cap_lift_period' src/fabric/api.py src/tok/api.py ; python3 <scratch>/vcap/one_corner.py off 0 for the four resolved wire values.

findings.detail: DEFECT 5 (asserting the Windows-vs-Steps conflict OPEN after the spine settled it) WAS REAL AND THE REWRITE IS TRUE OF THE TREE. All three of the old clauses are false now and I checked each: spine/derive.py::flush_period_windows exists, is declared beside flush_period, refuses anything but Windows, and spine/derive.py::flush_period still refuses anything but Steps -- so the conversion exists and the refusal it was added to protect is intact; the FAB.d_manage_period, FAB.d_cap_lift_period and TOK.d_cap_lift_period rows all call flush_period_windows(Windows(...), OPT.batch_windows); and there is no package TRAIN and no lever grow_cap_every. The report's 'not mine' note is also true: the identical stale paragraph survives verbatim in src/memory/levers.py::<module> ('THE CONFLICT WITH THE SPINE, stated rather than resolved ... there is today no legal conversion from a Windows-typed cadence to the flush clock'), plus a second echo further down the same file. That is MEM's row, not this audit's, and it is correctly left alone and named.
findings.repro: grep -n 'def flush_period\|def flush_period_windows' src/spine/derive.py ; sed -n '223,236p;278,288p' src/spine/derive.py for the two type refusals ; grep -n 'flush_period_windows' src/spine/assemble.py ; grep -n 'stated rather than resolved' src/memory/levers.py.

findings.detail: DEFECT 6 (the operating-population figure quoted at twice what the wire delivers) WAS REAL AND THE NUMBER IS NOW THE ONE THE WIRE DELIVERS. The old comment said 'the cull settling point FAB_PRESSURE x FAB_SLOTS (0.45 x 8192 = 3686 at the launch config)'; FAB.slots defaults to 4096 and FAB.pressure to 0.45, and the wire delivers 1844 on a live build. The direction the report gives is the one that matters: a soft cap of 3000 -- the value every sched_* arm used -- passes a check against 3686 and sits above 1844. One arithmetic footnote that does not change the verdict: spine/derive.py::operating_population takes the CEILING (0.45*4096 = 1843.2 -> 1844), so the old figure would have been 3687 rather than 3686 even at 8192; the corrected text quotes the old number only as a quotation, so nothing is wrong in the file.
findings.repro: python3 <scratch>/vcap/one_corner.py off 0 -> wires.d_operating_population = 1844 with FAB.slots=4096, FAB.pressure=0.45 ; sed -n '92,108p' src/spine/derive.py for the ceiling rule ; git show 8cb00e3:src/capacity/levers.py | grep -n '3686' for the pre-fix text.

findings.detail: DEFECT 7 (three DID IT FIRE names with no home, a RECORD TYPES line omitting two fields, and the eval/api.py item) WAS REAL AND ALL THREE PARTS ARE FIXED. `state_written`, `state_restored` and `state_refused` now appear only as counters KEYS ('cap.state_written' etc.) in capacity/api.py::state and capacity/api.py::restore, and the ledger dict they point at is the one capacity/api.py::new_valve seeds -- verified by grep and by reading Valve's field list, which contains no such attribute. The module's RECORD TYPES line now names `counters` and `gates` and no longer says '(P4 defines them)' of a record declared in that file; I counted the enumeration against dataclasses.fields(Valve) and it is 14 for 14. src/eval/api.py::curve_period now reads 'NOT A STUB, AND THE FOUR SIBLINGS ARE NOT EITHER -- DOM.manage_period, FAB.manage_period, MEM.rekey_period and CKPT.save_period', and I confirmed all four are stub-free bodies. The two collateral counts the report volunteered also hold: docs/04_CONTRACT.md says 'The **five** accessors' with its own note that it said 'four' until 2026-09-03, and there are EXACTLY 35 clock-unit levers across the registry (CAP 1, CKPT 1, DOM 4, EVAL 2, FAB 10, MEM 2, OPT 5, RUN 1, SIG 5, TOK 4).
findings.repro: grep -rn 'state_written\|state_restored\|state_refused' src/capacity/api.py ; python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'src'); import dataclasses, capacity.api as c; print([f.name for f in dataclasses.fields(c.Valve)])" ; the four sibling bodies printed by a small extractor over src/{domains,fabric,memory,ckpt}/api.py ; sed -n '2043,2046p' docs/04_CONTRACT.md ; and a registry walk counting levers whose unit is a spine.units.Clock subclass -> 35.

findings.detail: BEYOND THE REPORT: the off-by-one the audit fixed in src/eval/api.py::curve_period survives one package over, in the sibling that carries the same sentence. ckpt/api.py::save_period's body comment reads 'NOT A STUB, AND THE THREE SIBLINGS ARE NOT EITHER'; there are FOUR (EVAL.curve_period, DOM.manage_period, FAB.manage_period, MEM.rekey_period), exactly as docs/04_CONTRACT.md's 'five accessors' sentence implies. Those two are the ONLY occurrences of that sentence in src/, so the fix repaired one of a matched pair. It is CKPT's file, not this audit's, and the audit named the analogous MEM twin for its own DEFECT 5 -- naming this one too would have cost a line and left the tree with one place to look.
findings.repro: grep -rn 'SIBLINGS ARE NOT EITHER' src/*/api.py -> src/ckpt/api.py (THREE) and src/eval/api.py (FOUR).

findings.detail: BEYOND THE REPORT, and inside the helper the fix rewrote: `_resolve`'s one-line docstring is 'The sentinel, the operator, and the checkpoint, in that order of precedence.' The body's order is targets=='off' first, then the operator's explicit value (including an explicit 0, which the fix routed to the hard ceiling), then the checkpoint, then the default sentinel LAST. So the sentinel is named first and resolves last, and the branch that actually dominates -- 'off' -- is not named at all. Every other statement of the precedence in the file is correct (new_valve's own docstring, the two inline comments, and the origin strings), which is what makes the one-liner a live contradiction rather than a wording preference: it is the summary a reader skims. Pre-existing (identical in git 8cb00e3) and untouched by a fix that edited the two branches under it.
findings.repro: sed -n '172,210p' src/capacity/api.py -- the docstring line against the four returns beneath it; git show 8cb00e3:src/capacity/api.py | sed -n '/def _resolve/,/if given/p' shows the same line before the fix.

findings.detail: BEYOND THE REPORT: the fix to capacity/levers.py falsified a sentence in another file and nobody followed it. The CAP.d_expert_slots row's `why` still reads 'capacity/levers.py::<module> names this exact field as what CAP_FAB_START's 0 sentinel resolves to and :123 records that it is absent from this table.' The second half is now false in substance -- capacity/levers.py::<module> now says 'ALL FOUR WIRES NOW EXIST IN spine/assemble.py's COUPLINGS' -- and the line citation was already dangling before the fix (line 123 of that file was the DEFECT 3 heading at git 8cb00e3 and is a sentence about inline conversions today). The neighbouring CAP.d_vocab_slots row cites ':244' the same way, which now lands in the middle of the fab_start comment. It is the spine's file, not CAP's, so it is correctly untouched -- but a report whose own MEDIUM was 'a file that reports an absence for something present corrupts the ledger' owed this its one line. It is also the standing citation rule making its own case: both citations are FILE:LINE into src/, and both drifted.
